resources.string:
"Encodes H.264 and fires RTMP straight at Twitch — no SRT/SRTLA server of your own required.

The catch:
• no bonding — just one connection, no network-teaming superpowers
• network drops, stream drops — same as any bog-standard Larix/Streamlabs setup
• no OBS remote either — that needs a server machine standing next to you

Turn it on when: you don't have your own server, or rock-solid uptime isn't the point. Need bonding or the OBS remote? Switch this off and spin up your own server."
"Creator Dashboard → Settings → Stream → Primary Stream Key.\n\nGuard it like a password — anyone with this key can stream to your channel instead of you."
"No dice. Log back into Twitch above (needs stream-key access) and try again."
"Log into Twitch with the button on the left first."

"One IP to rule them all: the SRT server, srtla_rec (for bonding) and the OBS remote all live on this same machine. Change it here, it changes everywhere.

What to type:
• your computer's LAN IP (ipconfig → IPv4)
• or a cloud address (belabox, IRLToolkit)

The port on the right depends on bonding: on, it's srtla_rec's port; off, it's the SRT server's port."

"Your stream lands on the server as live/<name>. The player looks it up by that exact same name.

What to type:
• Latin letters, no spaces
• "phone" is modest, "super_mega_stream_3000" also accepted

The only rule: it has to match whatever the server/player expects."

"How many kilobits per second we burn on making things look pretty. H.265 does compression witchcraft, so cranking this up doesn't help much — past the recommendation the picture barely improves, but your phone gets hot and starts dropping frames.

How to pick:
• tap a preset below — we already did the math
• a still room forgives a low bitrate
• leaves rustling and people moving outdoors is the hungriest content there is"
"💡 Presets for %1$s·%2$s fps — tap to apply:"

"Teams up Wi-Fi and cellular into one party: packets run down every network at once, so if one takes a nap, the others carry the weight.

Turn it on when:
• you're streaming on the move and the network is flaky
• you've got two or three networks at once (Wi-Fi + SIM)

Video goes to srtla_rec instead of straight to the SRT port. At home, you can probably skip it."

"The secret knock on the door — AES encryption for SRT.

How to pick:
• empty — door wide open, fine for your own private server
• set — the server needs to know the exact same secret

Get it wrong and the server will act like it's never met you in its life."

"SRT's airbag: how much time a lost packet gets to be resent before we give up on it. More padding means a steadier picture, but your viewer watches further behind real time.

What to set:
• 2000 — the sweet spot, a couple seconds of delay with no glitches
• higher — for a weak or long-distance network
• under 500 — for adrenaline junkies only"

"Usually no need to touch this — live.twitch.tv auto-routes you to the nearest datacenter.\n\nWant a specific regional ingest for lower ping? Grab one from twitch.tv/ingest, format rtmp://<host>/app."

"A panel on the stream screen that bosses OBS around on your computer: scenes, going live, recording.

How to enable it in OBS:
• Tools → WebSocket Server Settings
• tick "Enable WebSocket server"
• port and password are right there, under "Show Connect Info"

It shares the host IP from above. Turned off, there's no icon and no settings to worry about."

"The same password OBS is using.

Where to find it:
• Tools → WebSocket Server Settings → "Server Password"
• or the "Show Connect Info" button

"Enable Authentication" unchecked in OBS? Leave this blank."
"Tell us where to send the stream — your own server, the cloud, or just scan a QR code. Everything else is already set up; tweak it later in settings."
"Sends the stream down every network at once — if one naps, the others carry it. Sturdier on the move. Video goes to srtla_rec, and the port on the right will change."
"Your computer\'s LAN IP (ipconfig → IPv4) or a cloud address (belabox, IRLToolkit)."
"Your stream lands on the server as live/<name>. Latin letters, no spaces."
